customManagers.description: Newest Keycloak minor the integration tests and the local docker compose run against. The oldest tested minor (26.0) and the compatibility probes stay pinned.

packageRules.description: Runtime dependencies ship to users: 'deps' commits show up in the changelog and trigger a patch release.
Merge minor and patch updates once they are three days old and 'CI result' is green: unit, integration (real Keycloak) and pack smoke tests guard them. Majors stay manual.
Pin and digest updates wait for a review: the release-age check does not apply to pins, and a digest update dates from the original tag, so a moved tag would pass at once.
The release workflow holds the publishing rights and no CI job runs its actions, so every change to it waits for a review.
Node versions (engines, .nvmrc, CI matrix) are a support decision and change together by hand.
@types/node follows the oldest supported Node major (engines.node), so the typecheck flags APIs only newer runtimes have.
MCP SDK packages are released together.
The admin client follows the Keycloak release it was built for, so both move in one PR.
A new Keycloak minor needs a human: the docs name the tested versions and earlier minors changed permission behaviour.
